model.title: Recognizing Community Organizations for Veteran Engagement and Recovery Act
model.meta: Veterans' Affairs Committee · Rep. Mike Bost (R-IL)

summary.text: The bill would direct the Department of Veterans Affairs to run a three-year pilot program that gives grants to mental health care providers serving veterans, including in-person and telehealth care. To qualify, providers would need at least three years of operating an outpatient mental health facility, state licensing, and accreditation from a recognized body. Grant money could be used to deliver and expand care, encourage veterans to enroll in VA health services, cover outreach, training, and program evaluation, and treat uninsured veterans or those not eligible for VA care, while barring fees to veterans and double billing. Grants would be capped at $1,500,000 per facility per year, with rules for rural and urban distribution and priority for underserved areas, and the VA would report results to Congress afterward. The bill would also authorize $20,000,000 per year for fiscal years 2027 through 2029 to carry out the pilot. The bill also would change the dates in the loan fee table for certain VA housing loans, replacing June 9, 2034 with July 24, 2034.
